pr_title: Add methods for getting and setting individual color channels for all color spaces.
pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes #7746 except for making them const which is blocked on const float arithmetic.

## Solution

Added a bunch more methods for getting and setting individual color channels for every color space.

## Changelog

### Added

- `X_Y` Get the Y value in linear X colorspace.
- `set_X_Y` Set the Y value in X colorspace.
- `with_X_Y` Returns this color with Y set to a new value in X colorspace.

For all the remaining channels and color spaces.
pr_comments:
For the docs on all the `set_` functions, it doesn't just return in the given kind, it also modified self.

I so much want to remove that file 🙁

issue_context.title: Add `const fn Color::hue`, `Color::saturation` and `Color::lightness` etc
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

When working with color palettes, you often want to match the hue/saturation/lightness of existing colors.

Matching these directly is a bit frustrating: there's no easy way to check "what hue is this".

## What solution would you like?

Add methods that parallel [`Color::r`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/prelude/enum.Color.html#method.r) for all other provided color spaces.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

You can work around this by storing a `const DARK_MODE_BACKGROUND_HUE` etc and using that repeatedly.
comments: not sure it's possible to have those functions as `const` as they will involve float operations when converting from one colourspace to another
Yeah we may get blocked on const float arithmetic for now. Still handy to have even if not const.

Hlsa and Lcha both have a lightness and hue values. What are your opinions on how we should differentiate in the naming. Would a simple `_hsl` or `_lch` suffix do? And if so, should this be added to all methods or only the ones with conflicts?
Hmm. I'd start with it on all of them
This is now obsolete, with the addition of bevy_color.

review_comments: The alpha setter method is shared across all color spaces with alpha, does it make sense to also share the lightness method across all color spaces that support lightness? (Assuming the scale is the same? If not, disregard)

Close but not the same
10 in lch is 10.588 in hsl
50 in lch is 46.27t in hsl

Hmm... This changes the current color space of the color when writing to a channel in a different color space, which I found a bit surprising.

~~I personally think it would be more intuitive if the color was converted, the channel replaced then the color converted back to the original color space...~~

~~But can I see how that could be problematic when changing color channels of spaces that are surjective with regards the current color space (e.g. changing an HSL channel of an RGB color)~~

**Edit:** Looks like the current `set_*()` methods already behave like that? So it's not unprecedented. Maybe we could document this behavior?

Added the following to the end of each doc comment for the setters.
```
returned value is of variant [`Color::XXX`]
```
Same for hue, if the scale is the same

Not the same.
[Some website that says so](https://lea.verou.me/2020/04/lch-colors-in-css-what-why-and-how/#:~:text=The%20hue%20angles%20don%E2%80%99t%20fully%20correspond%20to%20HSL%E2%80%99s%20hues.%20E.g.%200%20is%20not%20red%2C%20but%20more%20of%20a%20magenta%20and%20180%20is%20not%20turquoise%20but%20more%20of%20a%20bluish%20green%2C%20and%20is%20exactly%20complementary.)
